data.narrative:
Redwood Materials is a Series E climate and energy company founded by J.B. Straubel, currently valued at $6.0B+ on $2.125B raised. The relevant comp universe consists of nine private frontier-tech peers in Climate & Energy (including QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Enovix, and Amory) and one public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA).

Stage-progression methodology is applicable here, using the $6.0B last post-money valuation as the base and applying a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E to later-stage transitions, yielding $8.4B. The peer-median approach is not applicable: while seven Climate & Energy peers exist in the broader universe, the narrow filters (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier cohorts) yielded insufficient density—fewer than three datapoints in any filtered set. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the sector's heterogeneity.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $7.1B to $9.7B, with a median of $8.4B. This range reflects limited methodological diversity (one applicable method) and reflects the Stage E positioning between the current $6.0B mark and typical next-round step-ups. Key uncertainties include: the scarcity of tight peer comparables at this stage and valuation tier, precluding cross-validation; the sustainability of the 1.4x multiplier under current market conditions; and absence of sufficient public market data. Widened ranges are warranted until additional comp density or performance milestones emerge.
